To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new approach to speech recognition that uses deep neural networks to directly transcribe audio data to text.
• We have built the first speech recognition system that does not require an intermediate phonetic transcription.

1) the deep bidirectional LSTMs are a powerful architecture for speech recognition, 2) the CTC loss function can be modified to directly optimize the WER, 3) the WER can be reduced from 27% to 6% by combining the CTC network with a conventional baseline, and 4) the WER is reduced to 8% by adding a trigram language models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how well we can do speech recognition without the need of a phonetic transcription.
the problem of end-to-end speech recognition.

the development and evaluation of a novel speech recognition system that is based entirely on recurrent neural network models and that is capable of transcribing speech without requiring an intermediate representation of phonetic units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper is a good paper.

the system presented here is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the Wall Street journal task without any linguistic information, and is able to achieve a word error rate on a par with the best systems in the literature, with the addition of a language model.
the system achieves a word recognition accuracy of 93% and a character recognition accuracy of 98% on the Wall-Street-Journal dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed model is a strong contender for the state-of-the-art in speech recognition, and that it is capable of achieving the performance of a system with a large lexicon and language model without requiring these resources.
we have shown that a single, end-to-end model can achieve a state-of-the-art performance for a speech recognition system.

we are the first to show that a neural network system can achieve state-of-the-art performance on the standard speech recognition benchmark, without any hand-crafted feature extraction or linguistic knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recurrent networks can be trained to directly transcribe speech, and that the resulting system is competitive with the best existing speech recognition systems.
the deep bidirectional recurrent neural network architecture, with its ability to learn long-range context, is well suited to the problem of speech recognition.
a single, large, recurrent neural network is capable of performing the entire speech recognition process: acoustic, pronunciation, and language modelling.
